title: A locally quasi-finite morphism with quasi-compact source has universally bounded fibres (Stacks 03JA)
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and assume $X$ is quasi-compact. Then the fibres of $f$ are universally bounded: there is an integer $n\geq0$ such that for every $y\in Y$ the fibre $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field]) is a finite scheme over $\kappa(y)$, i.e. $X_y=\operatorname{Spec}B_y$ with $B_y$ a finite $\kappa(y)$-algebra, of degree $\dim_{\kappa(y)}B_y=\dim_{\kappa(y)}\Gamma(X_y,\mathcal O_{X_y})\leq n$. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Definition Tag 03J4 and Lemma Tag 03JA.)
